Serajul Huq with SAM Mahbub Elahi, Advocates ----- For the Appellants.

parties:
Kadu and others ----- Appellants
Vs. 
The State ----- Respondent
full_judgment: 14. PW 2 Yakub Ali, PW 4 Biddya Miah and PW 6 Jiban Ali are the eye-witness to the alleged occurrence. PW 2 stated that on 26th Chaitra, 1381 BS at about sun set when he along with Biddya Miah, Jiban Ali, Bisha Miah and deceased Asak Ali were returning from the hat with cart load of paddy and reached the road near the pagar to the west of the house of Fatik, the accused persons came out of the pagar with arms in hands. He further stated that appellant Kadu struck Asak Ali with katra in his left chest, appellant Sadu struck on the right side of the neck of Asak Ali by a ramdao, appellant Sunil struck with katra in the right side of the chest of Asak Ali and appellant Torab Ali struck Asak Ali on the left shoulder by lathi and as a consequence Asak Ali fell down on the ground. On hearing the cries of these eye-witnesses PW 9 Abdur Rashid and his wife PW 7 Bakshu Bibi came to the place of occurrence when the accused persons fled away. PW 9 along with his wife and others carried injured Asak Ali to his house. PW 2 went to the field on that day as a kamla of PW 9 Rashid. PW 6 is the Bagnipati of the informant who is the Bhatiza of the deceased. PW 4 Biddya Miah and PW 6 Joban Ali corroborated the evidence of PW 2 in material particulars by stating abat appellant Kadu struck Asak Ali in his left chest with a katra, appellant Sadu dealt a ramdao blow on the right side of neck of Asak Ali, appellant Sunil dealt a katra blow on the right side of the chest of Asak Ali and Torab Ali dealt a lathi blow on the left shoulder of Asak Ali. The injury allegedly caused by Sadu on the right side of the neck of deceased by ramdao, the injury allegedly caused by the katra on the right side of the chest of Asak Ali by appellant Sunil and the injury allegedly caused by the appellant Torab Ali on the left shoulder of Asak Ali were not found by the post mortem Doctor at the time of post mortem examination. This raised a doubt as to the alleged participation in the occurrence by the appellants Sadu, Sunil and Torab Ali. The post mortem Doctor found two stabbing wounds on the left side of the chest of Asak Ali and one of them was allegedly caused by katra blow by appellant Kadu. There is evidence to indicate who caused the other stabbing wound on the left side of the chest of the deceased. None of the appellants, according to the evidence on the side of the prosecution, inflicted the wound Nos. 1, 3, 4 and 5 as found by post mortem Doctor. These glaring inconsistencies between the existence of the injuries on the dead body of Asak Ali as found by the post mortem Doctor and the evidence of the prosecution witnesses about the injuries caused by the appellants irresistibly lead us to a conclusion that the occurrence did not take place in the manner as alleged by the prosecution and that persons other than the appellants caused those injuries as found by the post mortem Doctor on the dead body of Asak Ali which none of the prosecution witness saw. Admittedly PW 9 Abdur Rashid is step brother of the deceased and he took settlement of some land which was in possession of the appellants and appellant Kadu filed a case under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure against PW Rashid and another. The possibility that PW 9 Rashid falsely implicated the appellant out of grudge in the murder of Asak Ali cannot be altogether ruled out.
